column1: snob§The snob at the next table pronounced four wine names wrong and corrected the waiter on a fifth.§邻桌那个**势利眼**把四个酒名念错了，还纠正了侍者第五个的读法。§
soar§Applications soared from ninety to four thousand after a single broadcast, and the office had four staff.§一次播出后申请从九十份**飙升**到四千份，而办公室只有四名员工。§
socialize§The programme socializes new staff into habits nobody has examined in about forty years.§这个项目把新员工**同化**进一套约四十年无人审视过的习惯。§soci（同伴，同 society 社会）
solace§He found solace in the routine rather than the company, and walked the same four miles every evening.§他在常规而非陪伴中找到**慰藉**，每晚走同样的四英里。§solac（安慰）
solemn§The occasion was solemn for about nine minutes and then somebody's phone played a dance tune.§这个场合**庄严肃穆**了约九分钟，然后某人的手机放起了舞曲。§sollemn（庄重的）
solemnize§The union was solemnized in a registry office with four witnesses and no photographs at all.§这场结合在登记处**依礼举行**，有四名证人，完全没有照片。§
solicitous§She was solicitous about everyone's comfort and forgot, four times running, to eat anything herself.§她对每个人的舒适**关切备至**，却连着四次忘了自己吃东西。§soli（整体）+ cit（唤起，同 excite 激动）→ 全副心思都被牵动
solicitude§His solicitude for the family lasted long after the cameras left, which four of them mentioned later.§他对这家人的**关怀**在镜头撤走后仍持续很久，其中四人后来提到这点。§
solidify§Nine months of small agreements solidified into a partnership that neither side had planned.§九个月的小协议**凝固**成一段双方都没计划过的合作关系。§solid（结实）+ fy（使）
solitary§The solitary reader in the corner turned out to be the only person who had finished the report.§角落里那位**独自一人的**读者，原来是唯一读完那份报告的人。§sol（孤单，同 sole 唯一的）
solvent§The company was solvent on paper and unable, for nine weeks, to pay anyone at all.§这家公司账面上**有偿付能力**，却九周付不出任何人的钱。§solv（解开／偿付，同 solve 解决）
somber§The somber tone of the last four chapters is what makes the ending land as hard as it does.§最后四章**阴郁的**基调，正是结尾能砸得那么重的原因。§umbr（阴影，同 umbrella 伞）
somnolent§The afternoon session was somnolent until a question from the back woke the entire room.§下午的会**昏昏欲睡**，直到后排一个问题惊醒了全场。§somn（睡眠，同 insomnia 失眠）
sonorous§His sonorous reading of a dull document made four hundred people sit still for ninety minutes.§他对一份枯燥文件**洪亮浑厚的**朗读，让四百人静坐了九十分钟。§son（声音，同 sonic 声音的）
soothe§Nothing soothed the child until a nurse found the blanket that had come in with her nine hours earlier.§什么也**安抚**不了这孩子，直到一位护士找到九小时前随她一起送来的那条毯子。§
sophistication§The sophistication of the fraud was its undoing: only four people in the country could have designed it.§这场骗局的**精密老练**正是它的败笔——全国只有四个人能设计出它。§
sophistry§The argument is sophistry dressed as rigour, and it takes about four steps to see where it cheats.§这个论证是披着严谨外衣的**诡辩**，约四步就能看出它在哪儿作弊。§sophist（智者派）
sophomoric§The essay is sophomoric in the strict sense: confident, well-written, and wrong in four basic ways.§这篇文章严格说来是**一知半解的**——自信、文笔好，却在四个基本处出错。§sophos（智慧）+ moros（愚蠢）
soporific§The lecture was soporific and important, and about nine people in four hundred stayed awake for it.§这场讲座**催人入睡**而重要，四百人里约九人保持清醒听完。§sopor（沉睡）+ fic（做）
sovereign§The council is sovereign over four hundred hectares and has no power at all over the road through them.§这个议会对四百公顷土地**享有主权**，对穿过它们的那条路却毫无权力。§super（在上）→ 在上位者
spar§The two of them sparred for nine years in print and, in person, got on remarkably well.§两人在纸面上**唇枪舌剑**了九年，私下相处却出奇地好。§
spareness§The spareness of the prose is entirely deliberate: there are four adjectives in the first nine thousand words.§这些文字的**简省**完全是刻意的——头九千字里只有四个形容词。§
sparse§Data for those four years is sparse, and every conclusion about them rests on nine observations.§那四年的数据**稀少**，关于它们的每个结论都建立在九次观测上。§spars（散开，同 disperse 分散）
spate§A spate of resignations—nine in four weeks—told the board what the survey had not.§一连串**接二连三的**辞职（四周九人）告诉了董事会那份调查没说的事。§
spawn§The decision spawned four committees and nine subcommittees, and produced no discernible change in actual practice.§这个决定**催生**了四个委员会和九个小组，实践上却没带来任何看得出的改变。§
specificity§The specificity of the test is high and its sensitivity is not, which four clinicians misread.§这项检测的**特异度**高而灵敏度不高，四位临床医生误读了这点。§spec（种类，同 species 物种）
specious§The specious argument survived four rebuttals because it was shorter and easier to remember than any of them.§这个**似是而非的**论点熬过四次反驳，因为它比哪一次都更短、更好记。§spec（看，同 spectacle 景象）→ 只是看着好
spectacle§The spectacle cost nine hundred thousand pounds and was watched, in the end, by four hundred people.§这场**盛大场面**花了九十万英镑，最终有四百人观看。§spec（看，同 inspect 检查）
speculation§Speculation filled the four days before the announcement and was wrong in every particular.§**猜测**填满了公布前的四天，而在每个细节上都错了。§specul（观察，同 spectacle 景象）
speculative§The investment was speculative and the prospectus said so, in the ninth paragraph, in small print.§这项投资是**投机性的**，招股书在第九段用小字这么说了。§
spellbind§The old projectionist could spellbind four hundred children with a film he had shown nine hundred times.§这位老放映员能用一部放过九百遍的电影**迷住**四百个孩子。§spell（咒语）+ bind（束缚）
spontaneity§The spontaneity is rehearsed: he has told that story, in almost the same words, for nine years.§这份**即兴自然**是排练过的——他用几乎同样的措辞讲了那个故事九年。§spont（自愿）
spontaneous§The applause was spontaneous, which four hundred people can tell you and no recording can show.§这阵掌声是**自发的**，四百人能证实，而任何录音都显示不出来。§
sporadic§Sightings were sporadic for forty years and then, in one summer, there were nine.§目击记录**零星**了四十年，然后在一个夏天里就有九次。§spor（播种，同 spore 孢子）→ 撒得零零星星
sprawl§The city sprawls across four counties, and nobody is responsible for the roads between them.§这座城市**蔓延**过四个郡，而它们之间的道路无人负责。§
sprightly§The sprightly ninety-year-old outwalked four of us on a path we had all called easy.§这位**活力充沛的**九十岁老人在一条我们都说轻松的小径上走赢了我们四个。§sprite（精灵）
spurious§The spurious correlation held for nine years and vanished the moment someone controlled for income.§这个**虚假的**相关性维持了九年，有人控制收入变量后它立刻消失。§spuri（私生的）
squalid§The squalid conditions were reported four times before an inspector actually visited the building.§这些**肮脏不堪的**条件被举报四次，才有检查员真正到楼里去看。§squal（污秽）
squander§They squandered nine years of accumulated goodwill on a dispute over roughly four hundred pounds of shared costs.§他们为一场约四百英镑分摊费用的纠纷，**挥霍**掉九年积攒的善意。§
squelch§The rumour was squelched within four hours and had already reached nine hundred people.§这个传闻在四小时内被**压了下去**，而它已经传到九百人耳中。§
stabilization§Stabilization of the wall took nine months, and the crack that started it was four millimetres wide.§墙体的**加固稳定**花了九个月，而引发一切的裂缝宽四毫米。§stabil（稳固，同 stable 稳定的）
stagnation§Four decades of stagnation ended when a single employer arrived and hired nine hundred people.§四十年的**停滞**在一家雇主到来、招了九百人时结束。§stagn（死水，同 stagnant 停滞的）
stalemate§The stalemate lasted nine months and broke when one side simply stopped attending the meetings.§这场**僵局**持续九个月，在一方干脆不再出席会议时打破。§stale（固定）+ mate（将死，源自国际象棋）
standard§The standard was written in 1974 for equipment that has not been manufactured since 1994.§这项**标准**是 1974 年为一种 1994 年起就停产的设备写的。§
standardize§They standardized four processes and left the ninth alone, and the ninth is the one that fails.§他们**标准化**了四道工序，唯独放过第九道，而出问题的正是第九道。§
startle§The figure startled a committee that had been quoting a number nine times smaller for four years.§这个数字**惊到**了一个四年来一直引用小九倍数字的委员会。§
stature§Her stature in the field meant that four sentences from her could end a debate.§她在这个领域的**声望地位**意味着她的四句话就能终结一场辩论。§stat（站立，同 statue 雕像）
steadfast§His steadfast refusal to guess made him a slow witness and an unusually reliable one.§他**始终如一地**拒绝猜测，这让他成为一个慢却异常可靠的证人。§stead（位置）+ fast（牢固）
sternly§The judge spoke sternly to the prosecution and, in the ruling itself, agreed with them on four points.§法官**严厉地**训了检方，而在裁定本身中在四点上支持了他们。§
stickler§The stickler in the office insisted on the full procedure and, once in nine years, prevented a disaster.§办公室里那位**较真的人**坚持走完整流程，九年里有一次因此避免了灾难。§stick（坚持）
stifle§The culture stifles disagreement so effectively that four people resigned rather than raise an objection.§这种文化如此有效地**扼杀**异议，以致四个人宁可辞职也不提出反对。§
stilted§The dialogue is stilted for the first four pages and then, without warning, becomes wonderful.§前四页的对白**生硬做作**，然后毫无预兆地变得精彩。§stilt（高跷）→ 踩着高跷般不自然
stimulate§Four hundred pounds of prize money stimulated more entries than nine years of advertising had.§四百英镑的奖金**刺激**出的参赛作品，比九年的广告还多。§stimul（刺棒）
stimulus§The stimulus was small and the response was not, which is what made the finding interesting.§**刺激**很小而反应不小，这正是这项发现有意思的地方。§
stolid§His stolid manner in the crisis reassured nine hundred passengers who had every reason to panic.§危机中他**沉着不动声色的**做派安抚了九百名本有充分理由恐慌的乘客。§stol（愚钝）
strategist§The strategist who planned the campaign had never visited any of the four regions it targeted.§策划这场行动的**战略家**从未去过它所针对的四个地区中的任何一个。§
stratify§The rules stratify applicants into four bands, and about nine percent fall between two of them.§这些规则把申请人**分层**为四档，而约百分之九的人落在两档之间。§strat（层，同 stratum 地层）
streamline§They streamlined the process from nine steps to four and cut the average wait by three weeks.§他们把流程从九步**精简**到四步，平均等待时间减少三周。§stream（水流）+ line（线）
strenuous§Her strenuous objection was recorded in the minutes as "some discussion," which she is still angry about.§她**竭力的**反对在会议记录里被写成「有些讨论」，她至今为此生气。§stren（有力）
strident§The strident tone of the campaign lost it four supporters for every one it gained.§这场运动**尖锐刺耳的**调子每争取到一个支持者就失去四个。§strid（尖响）
stringent§The rules are stringent on paper and enforced, on the evidence of nine inspections, hardly at all.§这些规则纸面上**严格**，而从九次检查的证据看，几乎不执行。§string（拉紧，同 string 绳）
stunt§Four years of poor soil stunted the trees, and none of them reached half their expected height.§四年贫瘠的土壤**阻碍**了树木的生长，没有一棵长到预期高度的一半。§
sturdy§The sturdy little bridge carried farm traffic for ninety years and was condemned in a single afternoon.§这座**结实的**小桥承载农用车辆九十年，却在一个下午被判定报废。§
subdue§Four officers subdued him without injury, and the review still took nine months to complete.§四名警员在无人受伤的情况下**制服**了他，而复查仍花了九个月完成。§sub（在下）+ du ← duc（引导，同 conduct 引导）
subordinate§She subordinated her own project to his for four years and published, in the fifth, alone.§她把自己的项目**从属**于他的达四年，第五年独自发表了论文。§sub（在下）+ ordin（秩序，同 order 顺序）
